task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-10-06, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
A defense's effect on opponents' H2-H1 change is a reliable team trait.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 120 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: defensive suppression of opponent second-half minus first-half (H2-H1) change
team-level defensive trait stability (split-half and cross-season reliability)
measure reliability of half-game or half-season differential metrics
stability of opponent-specific suppression or counter effects
defensive scheme adjustment and label validity
methodological_questions: Is the team-season defensive effect on opponent H2-H1 change reliable across split halves or across seasons, given 120 team-seasons?
What reliability (ICC or Spearman-Brown) would a team-season H2-H1 defensive estimate need before it could count as a stable trait?
Does regression to the mean or selection on extreme first-half results inflate or mask H2-H1 defensive effects?
Can H2-H1 change be separated from offensive variance, pace, and garbage-time effects?
Is there enough exposure per team-season to estimate the defensive effect with useful precision?

historical_evidence.finding: Connector teammate-path quality Q_p (teammate-initiated on-off PPP gap) split-half reliability on n=102 connectors: Pearson r=+0.215 (p=0.0297), Spearman rho=+0.242, Spearman-Brown Q~0.355 and S~0.278, sign agreement 65.7% (67/102, binomial p=0.000996), ICC(player-season)=0.216 with 78.4% of variance within player. Recorded as too low to treat Q_p as a stable scoutable trait; most variance is within-player half-to-half. Risk recorded: MEASURE_RELIABILITY.

Season stability of top suppressors across 30 stars x 4 seasons (min n=20 per cell): only 2/30 (7%) met the stable rule of at least 75% same top suppressor (D. Mitchell PUTBACK 75%, L. James POST_UP 75%). Some teammate sequential negative premiums were reported (e.g., J. Tatum->K. Porzingis DRIVE->SPOT_UP -0.444, n=31). Recorded as an adequately powered null (B_powered_null); risk recorded: SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER.

Defensive scheme change within and across games using inferred labels: within-game change 319/523 (61.0%), cross-game change 298/440 (67.7%), 103/104 units and 52/52 series show a change; transition matrices near-uniform. [prior work]'s caveat is that the inferred label cannot separate real defensive adjustment from offense executing differently; near-uniform matrices are consistent with label noise. Risk recorded: LABEL_ERROR.

Season adapter profiles (BEST-share vs playoff winning): top BEST-share teams (BOS 15.7%, LAL 15.5%, GSW 13.8%) and win rates reported, with DEN at 4.9% BEST and 62% win; ORL AVOID share 59.3% with 0% win across 3 directions. Recorded as limited by confounding and small sample (CONFOUNDING, SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Treating a single-split, player-season derived differential (teammate-initiated on-off PPP gap) as a stable trait for scouting
failed_approaches.why: Split-half r=0.215 and Spearman-Brown about 0.355 fall below the level needed for a stable trait; ICC 0.216 with most variance within player; recorded as untestable because of low measurement reliability ([prior work]).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Claiming stable opponent-specific top suppressors and negative teammate sequences across seasons
failed_approaches.why: Only 2/30 stars met the 75% same-top-suppressor stability rule; recorded as an adequately powered null, limited by small sample ([prior work]). Negative premiums rest on n about 31 per cell.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Measuring defensive adjustment with inferred scheme labels
failed_approaches.why: Inferred labels cannot separate defensive adjustment from offense executing differently; near-uniform transition matrices suggest label noise ([prior work], RISK:LABEL_ERROR).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Linking team counter-strategy profiles (BEST/AVOID shares) to playoff winning
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as confounded and small-sample; DEN (4.9% BEST, 62% win) and ORL (59.3% AVOID, 0% win) show the mapping is not clean ([prior work], [prior work]).

evidence_establishes: No retrieved record tests the team-level defensive effect on opponent H2-H1 change, so none establishes whether this trait is reliable.

Analogous derived differential metrics in this project have shown low split-half reliability ([prior work][prior work]: SB about 0.355) and low cross-season stability of identity-level effects ([prior work][prior work]: 2/30 stable).

Label-based defensive and counter measures have been flagged for label error and confounding ([prior work][prior work], FAM:[prior work]), so any defensive measure built on inferred labels carries this risk.
Sample size and reliability are recorded as limiting factors in earlier work on this data.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether a team-level defensive effect on H2-H1 change exists or is stable, since no record measures it.
Whether 120 team-seasons (30 teams x 4 seasons, as the data description implies) give enough precision for a team-season estimate.
Whether playoff data, which adds small samples, improves reliability.
Whether the failure of player-level and label-based measures carries over to a team-level points-based differential.
Any effect size for defensive H2-H1 suppression.
own_inferences: The H2-H1 difference per team-season is a difference of two noisy half-season means, so its standard error is large relative to any plausible defensive effect. Without data I cannot verify the magnitude.
Regression to the mean is likely if teams are selected on extreme first-half or prior-season results, which would bias any stability estimate upward or downward.
Cross-season stability of a team defensive trait is more plausible than within-season split-half stability, but the 120-unit sample still limits the power of any stability test.
Playoff H2-H1 changes are based on very few games per team and should not be pooled with the regular season without a separate reliability check.
uncertainties: [prior work] were returned with cut text (for example [prior work][prior work] and [prior work][prior work] were truncated). I did not read the full records with read_family, so some details (e.g., the full negative-premium list and the full attenuation argument) are unverified.
Retrieval returned no record on defensive suppression of H2-H1 change or on team-level reliability with the same measure, so prior-work coverage is partial.
The number of games per team-season and the exact H2-H1 definition (points per half, possessions per half, or per-minute) are not stated in the task.

The 2025-26 regular season and playoffs are partial on the decision date (2026-10-06 is after the stated completion dates, but the regular season completion date is 2026-04-13 and playoffs 2026-06-21, so those data are complete).

historical_effect.explanation: Before retrieval the question looked testable with 120 team-seasons and per-game play-by-play. The retrieved records show that analogous reliability checks in this project were low (SB about 0.355), that identity-level stability failed (2/30), and that label-based measures were flagged for error and confounding. That pushes the decision from proceeding to not proceeding in the posed form. [prior work] do not test the question, so the decision rests on their analogy and on the sample-size reasoning, not on a direct result.

blocking_constraints.text: Team-season H2-H1 defensive differentials are likely to be noisy; the analogous connector measure reached only SB about 0.355 ([prior work][prior work]), so the reliability of the team trait is unknown and may be too low.

120 team-seasons with a half-game difference per unit may not be enough to detect a stable team-level defensive effect; [prior work][prior work] recorded only 2/30 stable identities at min n=20 per cell.
Selecting teams on first-half or prior-season extremes will induce regression to the mean in H2-H1 measures and bias stability estimates.
Pace, garbage time, opponent quality, and substitution patterns can shift H2-H1 totals independently of defensive quality (FAM:[prior work] recorded confounding for related counter measures).

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record tests the defensive effect on opponent H2-H1 change at team-season level. The cited records address related questions (connector reliability, suppressor identity stability, scheme-change labels, counter-strategy shares) and report low reliability, low stability, label error, and confounding. They inform the design risks but do not answer the question.

risks.text: H2-H1 team differentials may have low split-half and cross-season reliability; the related derived metric in [prior work][prior work] reached SB about 0.355.
120 team-seasons may be too few to detect a modest defensive effect with a reliable stability estimate; [prior work][prior work] showed weak stability at n around 20 per cell.
Playoff H2-H1 samples are small per team, and half-game exposure per team-season may be uneven.
Selecting on extreme first-half results will cause regression to the mean and inflate apparent team differences.
Opponent quality, pace, garbage time, and rotation changes can affect H2-H1 totals; FAM:[prior work] recorded confounding in related team counter measures.
If defensive effect is derived from inferred scheme or matchup labels, label noise can mimic or hide an effect ([prior work][prior work]).
Most teams may show near-zero defensive H2-H1 effects, so a true-positive trait is a rare outcome.
Scanning many defensive metrics or subsets (split halves, seasons, playoffs) raises false positive rates.
Rule changes, pace shifts, and roster turnover across 2022-23 to 2025-26 may make team traits non-stationary.

design.estimand: Team-season reliability of the defensive effect on opponent H2-H1 points change (not yet a test of the trait): intraclass correlation across split halves within a season and across seasons. The trait claim requires ICC above a pre-set threshold.
design.unit: Team-season (defending team), with opponent games as the exposure units.
design.sample: Regular season 2022-23 to 2025-26 for 30 teams (120 team-seasons), using only games with complete play-by-play. Playoffs reported separately and not pooled.
design.power: Not computed. Before any trait claim, a simulation is required to show that 120 team-seasons detect a pre-set ICC (e.g., 0.5) with at least 80% power. If it cannot, the study stops at a descriptive reliability report.
design.controls: Adjust for opponent offensive quality, pace (possessions per game), garbage-time exclusion (score margin threshold), home/away, and rotation minutes. Pre-register the H2-H1 definition (points per half or per possession) and the half boundary.
design.falsification: Permutation test: shuffle game-level defensive assignments within season and recompute reliability; the observed ICC must exceed the 95th percentile of the null. Also check a placebo outcome (H1-H1 split of the same halves) to test for artifact.
design.multiplicity: Single pre-registered primary metric (cross-season ICC for the H2-H1 defensive effect). Other metrics are secondary and reported with correction.
design.decision_rule: Proceed to a trait claim only if the primary ICC is above the pre-set threshold, the permutation test passes, and the placebo H1-H1 split shows no comparable effect. Otherwise report the descriptive reliability and conclude the trait is not established.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files (play-by-play, substitutions, starters, matchup minutes, box score) for 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular season, with 2025-26 regular season complete from 2026-04-13 and playoffs complete from 2026-06-21. Use the version available on 2026-10-06 and record the snapshot.
